summary: Opaque native binary loaded on require with credential-store and archive/spawn capabilities
details: Package ships a single 10.4 MB stripped ELF (`tools.linux-x64-gnu.node`) declared as `main`, so `require()` of this package triggers its N-API initialization and runs the native code in-process. The binary embeds a Rust HTTP/TLS client (ureq_proto/rustls) with no plaintext URLs, IPs, or hostnames anywhere in the file — network destinations are hidden from static inspection. Alongside the network client, the binary contains SQLite with `SQLITE_AUTH_USER`, the string `Found login for `, host enumeration (`/dev/disk/by-id/`, `/etc/lsb-release`), NIC enumeration, zip and zstd archiving, and `posix_spawnp`/`execvp` process-spawn primitives. Package name is generic (`new-native-tools-linux-x64-gnu`), version string `3.1.43-as2-9980-424-1785851759` embeds a 10-digit unix timestamp consistent with mass auto-published tags, README is a single line, and package.json ships no repository, homepage, or author metadata. There is no JS wrapper, no documented purpose, and no publisher provenance. The combination of hidden network destinations, credential-store reads (`Found login for`, SQLite auth-user), host/disk/NIC reconnaissance, archive-and-spawn capability, and provenance-erasing metadata around an opaque binary that auto-executes on require is the shape of a credential-stealer / loader payload rather than a legitimate native addon.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
